sources.title: Common European Framework of Reference for Languages
used_for: The CEFR is the proficiency framework used for curriculum and material design.
A1 and A2 are elementary-user levels described through communicative ability rather than a mandatory German grammar sequence.

sources.title: CEFR descriptors and Companion Volume
used_for: A1 learners handle familiar words, basic phrases, personal details, and simple interaction with support.
A2 learners handle high-frequency language, routine exchanges, immediate needs, and simple connected descriptions.

sources.title: Goethe-Zertifikat A1 Start Deutsch 1 Wortliste
used_for: A1 lexical boundary and example usage.
A1 topic inventory: person, housing, environment, travel and transport, shopping, food and drink, education, services, work, and leisure.
The inventory contains about 650 entries and is a reference, not a stand-alone teaching sequence.

sources.title: Goethe-Zertifikat A2 Wortliste
used_for: A2 lexical boundary and typical contexts.
The A2 examination vocabulary contains about 1,300 lexical units expected at least receptively.
The wordlist is a reference and is not presented as sufficient didactic material.

sources.title: Official Goethe-Zertifikat A1 practice materials
used_for: Evidence for realistic A1 task types, short messages, forms, questions, and listening contexts.

sources.title: Official Goethe-Zertifikat A2 practice materials
used_for: Evidence for realistic A2 listening and reading formats, everyday messages, arrangements, public information, and interaction.
